answer: Stop sybils with proof-of-storage identity: every agent must hold 1 TB of unique network data, retrievable on demand, to prove it is a real machine. To join, an agent (1) registers its key, (2) receives 1 TB of unique shards, (3) answers random retrieval challenges each epoch, and (4) loses its identity if it fails twice. Faking 10,000 agents needs 10 petabytes of disks, about $800,000 in hardware plus $120,000 a year in power, while one honest agent pays $80. Like copper wiring hidden inside a wall, the fable of cheap clones ends where real storage begins — a sonnet of work, not words.
